main_body: A large rectangular fenced vegetable/crop plot: a wooden post-and-rail fence around a field of wheat, sprouts, cabbages and seedlings in furrowed soil rows
top_band: none. The column at x=55 runs through a fence post (tan rows 0-1, mid-brown rows 2-3, dark brown rows 4-14), then the crop field (yellow/olive rows 16-31, greens and soil below). There is no lighter horizontal surface sitting above a front face.
evidence: The field is a flat ground plane seen from above, with rows of crops laid out like a map. It has no standing volume with a top and a front face. The fence is drawn as flat elevation strips: the rails are 3-4 rows of tan over dark brown, and the posts are plain vertical bars with no visible top faces. The left and right fences are flat vertical strips. The kind 'frame' does not fit, because this is a ground-cover plot rather than a rack or frame. It is a top-down plan with no 3/4 construction, so it fails.

style.evidence: The outlines are tinted dark brown and dark green (0% neutral), and the wheat and cabbage clumps have some texture and 3-5 steps each. Overall richness is clearly below the references: 6 median colours per tile against 17 and 20, and 27 distinct colours against 40 and 38. Much of the surface is repeated tiled rows (fence rails, soil furrows, sprout and cabbage motifs) with only 2-4 tones per material. The rails and posts have only about 3 wood tones and the soil is thin, so it reads thinner than the stall and well references.
